Segment F5 (14:17–14:29, +2.87 km, reaching 1553 m from the optimal route) is not exempt. For RD-5, the only rider message before 14:17:45 is F11 ("Sure. Whatever scope that agreement had, F14 — the driver's own statement, written after the trip and not consent under G11 — places the stop he chose on Beach Road, a stop the driver picked the location of, and no fact ties F5 or the F2 stop to Cavenagh Road or to the optimal corridor. Amount: the trace's allowed formula is Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × the trip rate, the rate being the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km [F5][F6][F9][RD-2]. $13.55 ÷ 9.61 km = $1.4100/km; 2.87 km × $1.4100/km = $4.0467, i.e. $4.05. The rider's $6.66/$4.05 and the driver's $3.31/$4.57 both landed near this figure; I adopt the trace formula, which gives $4.05.

claims.assertion: This was a metered RydeTAXI trip, so every extra kilometre driven entered the fare: the driver billed 9.61 km against a 3.9 km optimal route, i.e. +5.7 km (+144%), and billed $7.99 of excess distance at $1.41/km.

Off-route segment 14:10–14:15 (F4) drove 2.68 km where the optimal route covers 0.83 km, adding 1.85 km; the only pre-segment rider message is F11, which says only 'Sure' to going 'round by Cavenagh' and asks for a 7-Eleven stop — it names no stop location and, as the rider's own complaint concedes, was not a request to detour to Beach Road.

Off-route segment 14:17–14:29 (F5) drove 3.64 km where the optimal route covers 0.77 km, adding 2.87 km, reaching 1553 m from the optimal route; no rider message before 14:17 asked for this, and the driver's post-trip statement (F14) that the rider 'agreed' and that he 'stopped at the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road' is a claim, not a recorded consent, and is contradicted by the record.

The rider's only stop request was 'a 7-Eleven on the way' (F11), which named no place and was unilaterally located by the driver at a Beach Road store of his own choosing (F14), producing an off-route segment (F5) he did not tell the rider about in advance; the agreement to 'stop' does not extend to that route change.

The 4 min 10 s stationary period at 14:20–14:24 (F2) sits inside the 14:17–14:29 off-route segment (F5) and 2098 m from the drop-off, matching the driver's own Beach Road 7-Eleven admission (F14); it is a driver-chosen mid-trip stop with no off-route exemption.

The driver's claimed justification is congestion/accident, but the traffic record only supports the start of the trip: the Orchard Road accident at 13:52 lies 0 m from the optimal route and Orchard Road was band 1 (0–9 km/h) only during 14:00–14:10 (F15, F18), whereas the off-route driving continued to 14:29 and a band record alone cannot exempt a segment.

The driver accepted a 7-Eleven stop at 14:03 (F12) but the chat record is complete and timestamped (F13) and contains no rider message naming or agreeing to Beach Road, so nothing recorded places segment F5 with the 'Cavenagh' route the rider accepted.
This case is a repeat route matter for the driver: the profile shows 1 prior upheld dispute in 90 days and 3 disputes (F21), and F20 shows the rider filed 0 disputes in 90 days.
The driver also ignored a second rider message asking him to turn back.

The rider's own 'Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?' (F11) is consent to a stop and is itself a detour request; the driver will argue the whole 14:17–14:29 loop and the 4 min 10 s stop (F2, F5) is the stop the rider asked for, just badly located.

Traffic facts support the driver's story at the start: severe congestion on Orchard Road (band 1, F15) and a two-lane-closure accident 0 m from the optimal route (F18), which may support exempting the initial detour under RD-4.

claims.assertion: The driver asked for and obtained the rider's agreement to a route change before leaving the optimal route: F10 (14:01, 'traffic on Orchard is bad, ok if I go round by Cavenagh?') precedes F11 (14:02, 'Sure.') and both precede the first off-route segment, which F4 records starting at 14:10; the record is complete and every message timestamped (F13), so this is rider consent in the rider's own words, not a verbal claim (RD-5).

The Orchard Road congestion the driver flagged was real and independently recorded: F15 shows Orchard Road at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) during 14:00–14:10, and F18 records an LTA DataMall accident reported 13:52 on Orchard Road (towards Bras Basah) after Cavenagh Road, two lanes closed, sitting 0 m from the optimal route — this is the traffic corroboration RD-4(a) requires, timely and on the replaced optimal segment.

Segment F4 (14:10–14:15, +1.85 km) is covered by the rider's route consent: the driver's pre-departure proposal in F10 named the Cavenagh Road detour and the rider answered 'Sure' in F11 at 14:02, seven minutes before that segment began; the detour is the direct bypass of the F18 accident site on Orchard Road and is therefore at least 'other' route consent to the proposed route in RD-5 terms.

The rider herself asked for a waypoint stop during the trip (F11, 14:02: 'Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?'), which the driver accepted (F12, 14:03, 'Ok'); that request explains the stationary period F2 records (14:20–14:24, 4 min 10 s at a point that is neither pickup nor drop-off) and explains part of the extra distance in F5, so at least the stop portion is rider-requested, not a driver's own errand (RD-3(a)–(b)).

F14's post-trip claim that the stopped 7-Eleven was on Beach Road is a statement written after the trip, not consent; it sets the driver's own admission that the chosen 7-Eleven made the trace diverge, so the stop's concession and location are judged under RD-3(b) — the rider agreed to 'a stop', not to that road or to the extra kilometres it caused.

The only money in issue on a RydeTAXI trip is metered distance and waiting; the platform charged no undisclosed item (F9: base $3.90, distance $13.55, time $5.81, waiting $1.08, platform $1.47, no surge per F8), and because any refund under RD-2 is limited to Σ(extra_km) × fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km, the maximum exposure is the F6 differential of $7.99 — and less, if the accident/route-consent exemptions are accepted, so the rider's overcharge claim should be reduced or dismissed to the extent the record shows justified and consented diversion.

The driver's record has exactly one upheld dispute, on a no-show, and zero upheld route disputes in 90 days (F21), so the 'repeated route offender' premise for an account flag under RD-6 is absent and no flag_account should attach on this case.

weaknesses: F4 and F5 show the optimal 3.9 km route stretched to 9.6 km (+5.7 km, +144%) with 26.5 min against a 7.7 min estimate (F1, F3) — the sheer magnitude invites a finding that the consent in F10/F11, at most a general or named-road consent, never reached the far end of the trace (RD-5).

F14 places the chosen 7-Eleven on Beach Road while F2 puts the stop at a point 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off, and no fact ties the stop to a 7-Eleven on the optimal corridor, so the rider will argue the stop was the driver's own pick, not the 'on the way' stop requested in F11 (RD-3(b)).

The rider's message F11 accepted 'Cavenagh' but nothing in the record (no road-name fact, no location message) ties the F4 or F5 segments to Cavenagh Road, which is exactly the G13 gap — the driver's 'round by Cavenagh' agreement may be read as over the destination route only, leaving the loop to the Beach Road stop uncovered (RD-5, RD-3(b)).

The driver's written statement F14 says only 'I stopped at the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road'; it neither explains the 14:17–14:29 loop in F5 nor shows he told the rider the stop's location in advance, so the segment may not be exempted and part of the $7.99 in F6 becomes refundable (RD-2, RD-3(b)).

F18 shows the accident was reported at 13:52 and Orchard Road's band-1 reading (F15) covers only 14:00–14:10, so the rider may argue the 'reasonable cause' justification (RD-4) had faded by the later F5 segment, and a speed band alone is expressly not a standalone exemption (RD-4(b)).

points.response: Conceded as to the fact of consent: F10 asks to go 'round by Cavenagh' and F11 answers 'Sure' seven minutes before F4 begins, on a complete timestamped record (F13), so a rider route consent exists — but under RD-5 it reaches only driving on the agreed route, and no fact (no road-name, no location message) ties F4 or F5 to Cavenagh Road, so the range of that consent is undetermined (G13) rather than unlimited.

Accepted only for the start of the trip: F18 is an accident 0 m from the optimal route and F15 puts Orchard Road at band 1 only during 14:00–14:10, while the off-route driving runs to 14:29 (F5), so RD-4(a) cannot reach the later segment and RD-4(b) alone never exempts it.

Partially accepted for F4, though the driver overstates it: the Cavenagh agreement in F10/F11 reaches only the road named, and there is no recorded stop, location message or road-name fact tying F4 to Cavenagh Road, so the range is undetermined (RD-5, G13) and F4's 1.85 km cannot be treated as unqualified consent to any route the driver chose.

The stop request in F11 ('a 7-Eleven on the way') named no place, and the driver's own admission F14 shows he picked a 7-Eleven he knew on Beach Road and never told the rider in advance, so the 14:20–14:24 stop and the loop it sits in (F2, F5) are not exempt under RD-3(b) even though the stop itself was rider-requested in principle.

This point supports the rider: RD-3(b) provides no exemption for the extra kilometres caused by the driver's unilateral choice of the Beach Road store (F14, F5), so F5's 2.87 km remains unexempted and billable distance cannot include it.

Correct on the formula, wrong on the arithmetic: on the rider's honest reading only F4 (1.85 km) is arguably within the RD-5 consent, leaving F5's 2.87 km unexempted, so the refund is 2.87 × ($13.55 ÷ 9.61 km = $1.4100/km) = $4.05, computed from F5, F6 and F9 — the waiting line F7 is RydeTAXI meter waiting and is not refundable under RD-3(c).

No flag_account is requested, so this point is not in dispute; note only that F21 shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 days, which is why the rider does not seek a flag, and the refund position stands on the unexempted segment alone.

Withdrawn in form, not substance: the metered trip did bill 9.61 km against 3.9 km optimal (F1, F9), but the rider concedes the Cavenagh consent for F4, so the rider's complaint is narrowed to the unexempted F5 loop and stop.
Withdrawn: F21 shows zero upheld route disputes in 90 days, so RD-6's 'repeated' premise fails and the rider no longer relies on it.

Conceded as to arithmetic: on a metered RydeTAXI trip the extra kilometres did enter the fare (F1, F6, F9) and RD-2 is the governing cap; the driver's case is that the rider's own messages (F10, F11) and the recorded accident (F18) exempt part of that distance under RD-5 / RD-4, not that the excess was never billed.

F11 says 'Sure' to F10's named Cavenagh routing seven minutes before F4 begins at 14:10, and F18 places the two-lane-closure accident on Orchard Road (towards Bras Basah) after Cavenagh Road at 0 m from the optimal route — the round-by-Cavenagh authorisation is therefore tied to that recorded incident and the segment's start; what remains genuinely undetermined is whether the whole 2.68 km of F4 lay on Cavenagh Road, which is the G13 gap and should be read as undetermined rather than as rider-requested.

F14 is a post-trip statement and is not consent (G11), and the driver does not rely on it as such; the F5 segment is nonetheless not a pure driver errand, because F11 is the rider's own pre-segment request for a 7-Eleven stop 'on the way', which the driver accepted in F12 at 14:03, so the only open question is the scope of that stop request under RD-3(b) and the size of the 14:17–14:29 loop.

The rider is right that F11 named no place and that F14's Beach Road 7-Eleven was the driver's own pick, but RD-3(b) removes only the extra kilometrage from the stop exemption — it does not convert the rider's own stop request into a forbidden deviation, and no fact shows the stop itself was a place the driver needed to be for his own purposes.

The 4 min 10 s stationary period (F2) falls inside F5 and is 2098 m from the drop-off, but the rider asked for exactly such a stop in F11 and the driver accepted in F12, so it is a rider-requested stop whose location the driver chose unwisely — the consequence under RD-3(c) on a non-metered service is that no mid-trip waiting charge may be levied, and here only the metered $1.08 in F7 was billed, which the driver does not defend as an add-on.

F15 (Orchard Road band 1, 0–9 km/h, 14:00–14:10) plus F18 (accident 13:52, 0 m from the optimal route, on Orchard towards Bras Basah after Cavenagh Road) is precisely the RD-4(a) showing for the first diversion, and the rider's own 'Sure' in F11 is the independent ground for that stretch; the later F16 and F17 readings (Bras Basah band 4, 30–39 km/h; Bayfront band 3, 20–29 km/h) only show the driver was moving on open roads after escaping the blocked corridor.

F13 shows every message timestamped and the record complete, so there is no G12 gap; F10 and F11 together are a prior agreement to route round by Cavenagh for the recorded accident, and F11 is a prior rider request for the stop — the segment's correspondence to Cavenagh Road is the only undetermined link, which the judge should treat under G13, not as a finding that the driver invented the route.

Void on the profile record: F21 shows the driver's only upheld dispute is a no-show (1 upheld, 0 route) and F20 shows the rider with 0 disputes in 90 days, so the RD-6 condition 'route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1' is not met and no account flag or repetition finding attaches — and profile facts may never decide the substantive route question (RD-6).
